article.headline: Storm Austen Slams Ireland With Heavy Rain And Severe Flooding Warnings
article.summary: Ireland is under a nationwide yellow weather warning until 10am following the arrival of the year's first major storm.
article.body:
Storm Austen made landfall on Ireland’s south coast late Thursday evening, unleashing intense rainfall that swept from Munster and south Leinster into Connacht. The system, named after the first director of the Irish Meteorological Service, marks the first storm of the year to strike the country. As the storm tracks across the nation, officials are bracing for a busy bank holiday weekend with localized flooding already reported in parts of Munster and Leinster.

For residents and travelers, the current weather conditions present immediate risks. Keith Leonard, head of the National Directorate for Fire and Emergency Management, confirmed that local response teams remain on high alert to handle emergencies triggered by the downpour. The yellow warning, which covers the entire country, remains active until 10am as authorities monitor the impact of the rain on regional infrastructure.

The volatile weather pattern is expected to continue with little reprieve. Met Éireann reports that a second system, Storm Boelo, is scheduled to arrive on Saturday. This follow-up storm coincides with high tides, which heightens the threat of coastal flooding from significant storm surges and powerful waves. The west and northwest coasts are currently identified as the areas most vulnerable to these secondary effects.

Officials are currently conducting formal assessments to determine the full extent of the damage caused by the initial storm. Emergency services are coordinating with local authorities to manage potential flash flooding in low-lying areas during the upcoming bank holiday window.

article.headline: One goal away: Pirates seek CAF group stage berth against African Stars
article.summary: Orlando Pirates hold a 1-0 advantage from the first leg and need to avoid defeat Friday at Orlando Amstel Arena to reach the CAF Champions League group stage for the first time since last season's failure.
article.body:
Tshepang Moremi's 75th-minute goal in Gaborone gave Orlando Pirates a slender 1-0 first-leg victory, but the Soweto giants know Friday's return leg at Orlando Amstel Arena will test their nerve in a competition where they stumbled at the same hurdle last season.

The stakes are stark: Pirates need only avoid defeat to advance, while African Stars require a two-goal win to progress outright. A one-goal Namibian victory sends the tie to penalties. Head coach Abdeslam Ouaddou stressed the importance of patience and intelligent movement, telling players that "this season Orlando Pirates is a giant in Africa" with stakeholders expecting the club's return to the group stage.

Defender Tapelo Xoki acknowledged last season's disappointment has sharpened focus. "We learnt from our lessons from last season," he said. "We have a lead, but we are playing at home. For us, it's all about the energy tomorrow, getting through." Pirates' defensive record at Orlando Amstel Arena provides encouragement—they have conceded just twice this season, with only Durban City and La Cure Waves breaching their defence.

African Stars arrive as formidable opponents. The teams have met three times previously, producing just two goals, both by Pirates. In their 2018/19 Champions League preliminary-round tie, Pirates won 1-0 on aggregate. The Namibian side showed defensive discipline in the first leg, absorbing pressure for 75 minutes before Pirates scored, and they engineered a comeback against AS Mangasport in the previous round.

article.headline: Miranda Hart opens up about ME diagnosis that forced her off stage
article.summary: Celebrity Traitors star Miranda Hart revealed she was diagnosed with ME (chronic fatigue syndrome) in 2024, which prevented her from enjoying her career and left her fearing she would never walk again.
article.body:
Miranda Hart feared she would never enjoy a gentle walk again after her chronic health battle intensified. The comedian was diagnosed with ME (Myalgic encephalomyelitis), also known as chronic fatigue syndrome, in 2024, a condition that prevented her from pursuing her career.

ME is a chronic condition affecting multiple body systems, according to Doctor Amir Khan, who explained the illness on ITV's Lorraine show on Tuesday, 20 September. "ME is a chronic, serious condition that affects lots of parts of the body, including tiredness, the immune system, the brain function," Khan said. "Even a small amount of physical activity can flare up your symptoms."

Hart has also dealt with Lyme disease, which led to periods of being bedbound and housebound. On Celebrity Traitors, she spoke about how her health struggles affected her life. "I've had times in my life when I haven't had that, through illness, and it's brought up that silly, sensitive soul," Hart said, reflecting on the importance of connection and laughter. The emotional vulnerability she displayed on the show—particularly when her fellow contestant Joe Lycett was banished—resonated with viewers and fellow Faithfuls in the Scottish castle.

Hart's openness about her condition came as her odds of winning the BBC series improved to second favourite at 4/1, climbing the leaderboard following episode six.

article.summary: Tyler Herro makes his home debut for the Milwaukee Bucks against the Chicago Bulls on Wednesday at 4:10 p.m. ET after scoring 24 points in Milwaukee's 128-116 loss to Washington, while the Bulls arrive fresh off a 135-92 rout by Toronto.
article.body:
Tyler Herro's return to his home state figures to draw attention Wednesday night at Fiserv Forum. The Milwaukee product, acquired in the Giannis trade, scored 24 points and nine assists in the Bucks' season-opening loss to Washington. Now he faces Norman Powell, the All-Star signing who was supposed to share Miami's backcourt with Herro last season but never consistently played alongside him due to injuries.

The Bucks are without Giannis Antetokounmpo on the roster for the first time since the 2012-13 season. Head coach Taylor Jenkins looks to bounce back after his team surrendered a 128-116 defeat despite leading 96-90 in the fourth quarter. Jaime Jaquez Jr. added 22 points and seven rebounds in that loss.

Chicago arrives bruised. The Bulls suffered the most lopsided defeat in a season opener in franchise history, losing 135-92 to Toronto while giving up 43 first-quarter points. Matas Buzelis led Chicago with 17 points, but rookie Caleb Wilson scored 16 while committing nine turnovers. Point guard Josh Giddey managed only 1-for-10 shooting and is probable with a wrist injury. Zach Collins is also probable with a right quadriceps strain.

The Bucks trail Chicago 138-137 all-time in regular season meetings but won three of four last season, capturing both home contests. Chicago's most recent victory came March 1 with a 120-97 win, as Giddey posted a triple-double.

article.headline: Winnipeg Jets actively negotiate Connor Hellebuyck trade to New Jersey Devils
article.summary: The Winnipeg Jets are currently working to finalize a trade sending three-time Vezina Trophy winner Connor Hellebuyck to the New Jersey Devils.
article.body:
The 33-year-old goaltender’s unpaid team suspension expired on Friday, officially clearing the path for the organization to finalize his departure. Hellebuyck, who holds a 345-208-55 career record with 45 shutouts, confirmed in late August that he requested a trade several months ago, citing dissatisfaction with the team's trajectory following the 2025-26 season. Winnipeg General Manager Kevin Cheveldayoff is reportedly prioritizing a trade solution to resolve the ongoing standoff before the goaltender returns to the active roster.

This potential move represents a major transition for both the franchise and the player. Winnipeg, which saw its performance drop from 116 points to 82 last season, must now navigate the departure of a player who has been a cornerstone of their defense. For the Jets locker room, the trade discussions aim to resolve a situation that captain Adam Lowry described as something they would have to handle with water-under-the-bridge conversations if the goaltender were to remain.

According to reports from Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman, the discussions with the New Jersey Devils have intensified as the suspension lifted. TSN Hockey Insiders Darren Dreger and Chris Johnston noted that both parties are considering delaying the mandatory physical examination to ensure the team's Heritage Classic against the Montreal Canadiens on Sunday remains the primary focus. While the team started the season with a 4-3-2 record in his absence, the organization remains intent on concluding the trade process after the weekend concludes. Hellebuyck is currently in the third year of a seven-year contract with an $8.5 million salary cap hit.

The Oilers star hit the threshold by recording four points during his team's matchup against the Carolina Hurricanes, including a critical goal in the third period that tied the game 5-5. This performance also marked his third five-point game of the young season, an achievement shared only by Lemieux in league history. 

This early production places McDavid on a statistical trajectory for 260 points this season, far exceeding his previous career standards. Beyond individual accolades, the Oilers have utilized a strong team structure under head coach Mike Babcock to maintain a 7-1-1 record, a start mirroring the 1983-84 campaign that preceded the franchise’s first Stanley Cup era. The team remains undefeated on the road, with significant supporting contributions from Evan Bouchard, who leads NHL defensemen with 18 points, and Leon Draisaitl, who has tallied 16 points and eight goals.

According to Sportsnet, McDavid’s consistent output has included 23 assists and eight goals through his first 10 appearances. The Globe and Mail notes that the Oilers' only regulation loss occurred against the Utah Mammoth, while their season opener was an overtime defeat to Vancouver. Goalie Devon Levi, filling in for the injured Freddie Andersen, has recorded a 5-1 record to bolster the Oilers' defensive efforts.

Looking ahead, the Edmonton Oilers will continue their five-game homestand at Rogers Place. The team is scheduled to host the Toronto Maple Leafs this coming Saturday in a nationally televised game.

article.headline: Bournemouth Rout Seven-Time European Champions Milan In Historic 3-0 Europa League Victory
article.summary: Bournemouth secured a 3-0 win against 10-man AC Milan in the Europa League after Mike Maignan was sent off for a first-half confrontation.
article.body:
Bournemouth boss Marco Rose witnessed his side dismantle seven-time European champions AC Milan in a 3-0 masterclass that moves the Cherries to a perfect three-from-three record in the Europa League. The victory was defined by a chaotic first half that saw Milan captain Mike Maignan receive a red card for shoving Tyler Adams in the face, a reckless moment that allowed the hosts to dominate the match. Justin Kluivert converted the first penalty following a Koni De Winter handball, while Marcus Tavernier calmly slotted home the second after the Maignan incident. Amine Adli capped the performance with a precise free-kick that sailed through a fragile Milan wall. 

For Bournemouth, this result marks a monumental milestone in their first-ever European campaign, proving they can compete at the highest level despite their modest history. The tension of the night extended beyond the pitch, as heated exchanges occurred between members of the Italian club's staff and several Bournemouth players, including Adam Smith. Even manager Marco Rose engaged in a sideline argument with Ruben Amorim's staff, underscoring the intense frustration of the visitors during their dismal return to England.

Amorim, now struggling to overcome the south coast side, has failed to secure a win against Bournemouth in five attempts. The Cherries entered the match with renewed confidence following their first Premier League victory of the season against Sunderland just days prior. As the club climbs the Europa League table, the focus remains on sustaining this momentum. Rose praised his squad for their brilliant performance from the first minute to the last, noting that the team handled the pressure of playing against 11 men and the subsequent man-advantage with total composure, securing a treasured scalp that will be remembered by their supporters for years to come.
